papers.title: ARRANGE: Agentic Skills for Layering Vocals
papers.abstract: Adding a singing voice to an existing piano recording requires decisions about melody, syllable placement, pronunciation, timing, and vocal register. ARRANGE organizes this work as a sequence of agent skills with readable intermediate artifacts and composer approval checkpoints. An LLM translates instructions in plain English, notes played on a keyboard, and vocal references into local edits; deterministic scripts validate and apply those edits before open audio models render the result. The Score Canvas makes note, syllable, and pronunciation decisions inspectable and editable. In a benchmark of 16 revision requests, three draws per request, and five LLMs, typed edits achieved exact-change correctness of 0.83-0.98, compared with 0.33-0.69 for whole-plan rewriting without ARRANGE instructions. A separate score-editing benchmark and a first-person worked example examine the interaction between representations and corrections. Author listening evaluations further explore voice transfer and register selection, including 185 listening presentations across eight copied voices. These evaluations support the value of constrained editing and expose limits of both model execution and listening measures. The contribution is an interaction architecture for retaining musical decisions through inspectable intermediate representations, rather than a new singing model or evidence of general usability.

papers.title: EVis+: Literature-Grounded Visual Analytics for Hypothesis-Driven Geoscientific Data Exploration
papers.abstract: Scientific researchers often interpret observational data in light of prior findings reported in the scientific literature. However, scientific literature typically remains external to visual analytics environments, requiring researchers to manually connect published findings with the data and hypotheses under investigation. In this paper, we present EVis+, a literature-grounded visual analytics system for condition-event time series analysis in geoscience. EVis+ enhances observational data exploration by retrieving and synthesizing literature-derived insights relevant to the dataset and analytical goals, transforming user-selected insights into testable hypotheses and mapping them to domain-specific visualizations through expert-curated templates, and supporting evidence examination, discrepancy validation, and literature-driven re-exploration to support iterative hypothesis refinement and scientific exploration. Rather than handing scientific analysis to an unconstrained language model, EVis+ uses structured AI-assisted transformations that keep intermediate results visible, allowing researchers to inspect and guide the analysis at each step. We evaluate the system through an evidence-grounding audit, a structured expert assessment of the insights, and case studies with geoscientists and a comparative study with domain experts.

papers.title: DataRecycle: Trustworthy Distillation of Structured Data from Scattered Web Evidence
papers.abstract: The web contains vast amounts of scattered quantitative evidence that is difficult to organize into comparable and verifiable structures. Yet its unstructured, sparse, and sometimes conflicting nature makes a systematic distillation costly and error-prone. Existing approaches force users to make a trade-off: search engines return document lists that require labor-intensive extraction and reconciliation, while generative AI systems produce fluent summaries that obscure data provenance, introduce reporting bias, and hide inconsistencies. We present DataRecycle, an interactive system that helps transform scattered web evidence into structured tables of comparable numerical facts. Given a user's query or statement, DataRecycle decomposes it into entities and attributes, retrieves candidate evidence, and organizes scattered, potentially conflicting records in a table-based evidence view. To address key challenges in automated data distillation (i.e., incomplete retrieval, untraceable generation, sparse data distribution, and multi-source inconsistency), DataRecycle adopts an ontology-guided, top-down data acquisition strategy, visualizes the recorded lineage from retrieved snippets to extracted values, and aligns heterogeneous data across dimensions such as time, definition, and scale. We evaluate DataRecycle through module-level experiments, a usage scenario, and a user study, showing that the system helps users organize numerical web evidence into provenance-linked tables and inspect uncertainty and conflicting sources.

papers.title: Inclusive Hand Pose Estimation via Topology-Aware Distillation and Progressive Kinematic Reasoning
papers.abstract: Hand pose estimation aims to recover the spatial configuration of hand joints from visual observations and serves as a fundamental perception module for downstream systems that rely on complete and topologically consistent hand representations. Most existing methods are developed under the assumption of fully articulated hand structures and tend to produce unstable or implausible predictions when parts of the kinematic structure are persistently absent, resulting in degraded performance or even system failure despite available partial observations. To study this challenge, we construct IncNYU, a physiologically constrained benchmark that simulates structural incompleteness through morphological modification of complete hand models and retains reference locations for both intact and synthetically removed regions. Based on this benchmark, we propose InsHaPE, an Inclusive Hand Pose Estimation framework designed to remain robust under structural incompleteness while preserving performance on standard, fully articulated hands. Built on hierarchical kinematic modeling, InsHaPE introduces two complementary components. First, a topology-aware distillation strategy transfers joint-level and relational priors from fully articulated hand representations, providing anatomically consistent initialization under missing structures. Second, a progressive kinematic reasoning module performs structured inference along the kinematic chain, enabling complete and anatomically consistent pose estimation under severe structural variations. Extensive experiments on NYU/IncNYU, together with external validation on MSRA, demonstrate that InsHaPE improves robustness under structural incompleteness while maintaining competitive performance on complete hands. System-level evaluations further show that InsHaPE improves robustness for downstream applications that require fixed-topology hand pose representations.

papers.title: SenFabric: 3D Printing On-fabric Sensing Mechanisms for Smart Textiles
papers.abstract: We present SenFabric, a one-step fabrication technique that 3D prints conductive TPU directly onto existing fabric. Rather than compensating for conductive material instability, SenFabric uses geometry-driven resistive structures in which motion changes conductive contact and reconfigures the effective path, producing characteristic signal responses that remain distinguishable despite variation in absolute resistance. We introduce four sensing primitives, slide, press, stretch, and bend, with geometric variables that control activation force, deformation range, and resolution, and a browser-based tool that adapts them to user-supplied outlines and generates routing, pins, and printable models. Four applications demonstrate wearable sensing, human-robot interaction, garment interfaces, and animal wearables, while evaluations show geometry-dominated sensing, cross-motion selectivity, and stable response under repeated use.

papers.title: "What Should I Do?" Guidelines for Responsibly Integrating AI in Software Engineering
papers.abstract: Speculations abound about the "right" ways for developers to integrate AI into their software engineering (SE) work, but the evidence that exists is sparse and contradictory. Yet, developers are held responsible for the products they ship with (or without) AI's help, so they need to integrate AI in responsible ways. To address this gap, we conducted a two-phase, large-scale investigation with 1,118 developers at Microsoft, GitHub, and Pfizer. In Phase 1, we surveyed 860 developers at Microsoft on where they sought and resisted AI support in their daily work, and from their accounts, synthesized 35 developer-facing guidelines: 29 across five categories of SE work and 6 cross-cutting ones. A year later, as AI capabilities and developers' experiences co-evolved, we validated them in Phase 2 with 258 developers in technology (Microsoft, GitHub) and biopharmaceutical (Pfizer) domains. Developers in our study found the guidelines clearly worded (92%) and relevant to their work (91%), and most wanted to adopt them in their own work (89%). We also report how developers described operationalizing these guidelines in practice: using AI to refine their craft and delegate verifiable work, while keeping judgment and accountability for themselves. For relationship-centric work, endorsement varied with developers' domain and their SE and AI experience. Overall, we offer concrete advice from in-the-trenches developers to other in-the-trenches developers, and a shared vocabulary that engineering teams can adopt to integrate AI well in their work.

papers.title: MB-SSIM: A Multi-Band Variant of SSIM, Tunable to Viewing Conditions
papers.abstract: SSIM, as practically deployed, contains a hidden two-band model: although it was introduced as a departure from channel-based vision models, it amounts to a product of one similarity functional applied to a low-pass and a high-pass version of the two images. This split, however, is defined in pixels, so the spatial frequencies each band covers, as seen by the viewer, change with the display and the viewing distance. Making the model explicit and expressing it in cycles per degree gives a version of SSIM that takes the viewing conditions into account while preserving its simplicity. The resulting metric, MB-SSIM, keeps SSIM's per-patch product of similarity ratios; the bands are placed where psychophysics places the visual system's channels, and the viewing geometry enters through a single number, the angular sampling density in pixels per degree. On the CID:IQ dataset, which rates the same 690 images at two viewing distances, one set of sub-band weights fitted jointly and evaluated on held-out content reaches a pooled PLCC of 0.834 against 0.787 for SSIM and 0.808 for MS-SSIM; on LIVE Release 2, calibrating the geometry yields 0.956 against 0.946 and 0.950. As a cross-verification, the CID:IQ weights applied unchanged to the Brightcove-Kingston multi-screen video dataset, which rates the same clips on a television, a tablet and a phone, give a pooled PLCC of 0.844 across devices where SSIM and MS-SSIM, which must return one number per clip, fall to 0.62 and 0.59. Accuracy is flat from three channels to six and insensitive to filter shape, window and peak placement; only the channel bandwidths matter, and the psychophysically measured values are a safe choice. The most sensitive parameter is SSIM's own stabilising constant: reducing it to a third raises the pooled PLCC to 0.857. Source code reproducing the results is available.

papers.title: Health Ikigai: Semantic Conversational Interfaces for Wearable Health Data to Support Behavioral Change for Senior Indian
papers.abstract: In ubiquitous health contexts, wearable feedback is often encountered in brief, interrupted moments of everyday life. However, many wearable and mobile health systems still present personal health data through numerical dashboards, leaving users and health coaches to interpret trends, thresholds, and deviations on their own. This interpretive burden may be especially relevant for adults aged 50-65 in India, where digital literacy, health literacy, language, and daily routines can shape how health technologies are understood and used. We present Health Ikigai, a design-oriented proof-of-concept framework that reframes wearable activity feedback from dashboard-based numerical interpretation to semantic conversational feedback. The prototype transforms replayed wearable-derived activity data into baseline-aware triggers, plain-language feedback, limited-turn conversational prompts, and coach-facing review summaries. A preliminary formative evaluation with ten adults in India suggests that participants perceived the interaction as understandable, lightweight, supportive, and actionable. We discuss design implications for low-burden wearable health interfaces that preserve coach oversight while reducing users' interpretive work.

papers.title: Postpartum Sense-Making and AI in a Fragmented Care System
papers.abstract: Postpartum women must navigate health information across a fragmented landscape of clinicians, peers, online communities, influencers, and, increasingly, large language models (LLMs). Existing evaluations of LLMs in health contexts primarily ask whether systems provide accurate, safe, and readable information. We argue that these criteria, while essential, are insufficient for understanding how LLMs may affect postpartum care. LLMs enter an information ecology in which women are already required to reconcile competing forms of expertise, determine whether their experiences are normal or concerning, and decide when and where to seek care. At the same time, online representations of motherhood and femininity shape which postpartum experiences are made visible and what forms of self-management are expected of women. Drawing together research on postpartum care gaps, online help-seeking, influencer cultures, gendered responsibility, and AI-supported health information, we position LLMs as emerging intermediaries within this broader care infrastructure. We argue that evaluating postpartum AI requires examining not only information quality, but also how these systems shape epistemic coordination, transitions to formal care, and the distribution of responsibility for making fragmented systems of care work.

papers.title: "I feel like AI is just everywhere": A longitudinal qualitative study on parents' perceptions, use, and mediation of GenAI
papers.abstract: GenAI has developed rapidly over the last few years, yet few longitudinal studies exploring how individuals' experiences with GenAI have changed over time exist. Even fewer studies have focused on families with children, despite the opportunity to explore how parents have balanced their needs, their children's development, and the fast pace in which technology changes. To better understand how parents' perceptions, use, and mediation of GenAI shifted over two years, we interviewed 10 parents who had participated in a prior study about their families' experiences with GenAI. Parents had shifted from thinking GenAI was novel to feeling like it was unavoidable, characterizing GenAI as a limited tool to believing GenAI development needed to be regulated, and focusing on their personal mediation strategies to wanting systemic plans to curb GenAI's long-term consequences. We position our findings within the context of parental mediation of technology and increasing collective mitigation of GenAI-related risks.

papers.title: When Being Wrong Is Right: Reverse-Capability Audio CAPTCHAs through Psychoacoustic Design
papers.abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have recently been shown to bypass audio CAPTCHAs designed around limitations of automatic speech recognition. To address this threat, we introduce reverse-capability verification, a general CAPTCHA framework that reverses the conventional human-easy, machine-hard relationship with respect to the physical ground truth. It selects challenges in which stable human perceptual limitations cause the human-reference answer to differ from the physical ground truth, while machine analysis tends toward that truth. Because the verifier accepts the human-reference answer, advanced solver capabilities and resulting improved recovery of the physical ground truth may instead strengthen the human-machine separation. We instantiate the framework through psychoacoustics and design two audio CAPTCHAs: HIPI, a classification task, and YINGCHEN, a counting task, together with their conjunctive composition. Across seven LALMs and eight attack strategies, the maximum observed machine acceptance rates are 19%, 17%, and 3% for HIPI, YINGCHEN, and their composition, respectively, compared with 45-100% for nine prior schemes. A multidimensional human usability study yields corresponding human acceptance rates of 78%, 90%, and 76%, while maintaining competitive efficiency and satisfaction. Further analysis demonstrates that advanced LALMs tend toward physical ground truth. These results show that reverse-capability verification substantially reduces machine acceptance while retaining high human acceptance through an approach different from conventional CAPTCHAs.

papers.title: SkillLens: An Interactive Human-LLM System for Diagnosing and Refining Agent Skills
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on reusable skills, yet maintaining them requires developers to connect revisions with changes in behavior and task outcomes. Existing workflows fragment evidence across versions, evaluation cases, and execution traces. We present SkillLens, an interactive human-LLM system for diagnosing and refining agent skills. A formative study with five developers and researchers identified challenges in prioritizing failures, reconstructing case-level evidence, and preserving context across revisions. SkillLens links performance changes, case transitions, skill diffs, invocation sequences, traces, and outputs in a recoverable workflow, while keeping model-generated explanations and refinements under human review. Through a between-subjects user study with 20 participants, we show that SkillLens supports developers in diagnosing and refining agent skills through a more usable and less demanding workflow than the baseline. These findings highlight the value of linking version comparisons, case-level evidence, and human-reviewed refinement across skill iterations.

papers.title: PatchLens: Adapting Mechanistic Interpretability Techniques for Non-Expert Audiences
papers.abstract: A chat interface presents a reply as finished text, concealing a model that predicts at every position and reruns. Mechanistic interpretability can show how a large language model produces text, but its tools are built for researchers. We present PatchLens, a browser interface that runs logit lens and activation patching on remotely served research-scale models. Each layer's state appears as the tokens it comes closest to, laid out by layer and input position; an intervention is a drag from one cell onto another. The tokens a learner reads are the tokens they manipulate. In a between-subjects study with 61 non-experts, the comparison against Transformer Explainer was inconclusive on post-test knowledge. PatchLens participants wrote their own prompts (21 of 32 against 1 of 29), reported lower mental demand, and located their difficulty in the interface rather than the material. We read the null as evidence about what such an instrument measures.

papers.title: Who Gets Blamed for the Blackout? A Critical Incident Analysis of Clients, Reputation Systems, and Online Freelancers
papers.abstract: Online labor platforms such as Fiverr and Upwork judge freelancers by how fast they reply, whether they deliver on time, and what clients say about them. In the Global South, these signals depend on electricity and internet connections that workers do not control. This paper asks how infrastructure failures, such as power outages, internet failures, and government internet shutdowns, become lasting reputational penalties in the gig economy, and how freelancers prevent or repair them. We use the critical incident technique to analyze 149 incidents from 30 interviews with online freelancers in Bangladesh, including accounts of the July 2024 nationwide internet shutdown. Most breakdowns were absorbed without lasting harm. Of the 21 that became lasting penalties, 17 passed through clients. A client who could not see the power cut or the shutdown read the worker's silence as unreliability and left, canceled, or gave a bad rating. Platform reputation systems then stored that judgment without its context. We call this two-stage process client-mediated misattribution. Freelancers responded with four repair strategies: making the context visible, making the breakdown invisible, staying visible to the platform, and reducing dependence on any single platform or client. Exposure and the capacity to repair were unequal, and urban participants were the most exposed. The study extends research on algorithmic management, attribution in distributed work, and information and communication technologies for development (ICT4D), and it proposes outage-aware design for platform rating and reputation systems.

papers.title: Feedback-Driven Prompt Refinement for Educational AI: Affective Trajectory Estimation and Bloom's Taxonomy Classification
papers.abstract: Contribution: This study has shown that a shared prompt-refinement procedure, guided by distinct affective and cognitive feedback signals, can improve held-out reference agreement and multi-label classification while reducing affective-generation variability without executor parameter updates. Background: Industry 4.0 has increased demand for personalized technical education across interconnected computing and engineering domains, while prompt sensitivity and generation variability have complicated dependable interpretation of instructional dialogue and learning outcomes. Research Questions: The study has examined whether task-specific feedback can improve affective-reference agreement, generation consistency, and cognitive classification without updating executor parameters. Methodology: A secondary language model has revised executor prompts using executor-output discrepancies against model-generated affective references for four dialogues and annotated Bloom labels for 70 learning outcomes; separate sets of 100 EduTalk conversations and 1,000 outcomes have supported held-out comparisons. Small refinement sets, unvalidated affective references, and absent learner-outcome measures have constrained interpretation. Findings: Affective mean absolute error has decreased from 0.742 to 0.702 and mean generation standard deviation from 0.307 to 0.238, while Bloom micro-F1 has increased from 0.687 to 0.893 and exact-match subset accuracy from 0.418 to 0.636. These findings have supported prompt refinement as a candidate approach for developing adaptive technical instruction, while its effects on workforce learning remain to be established.

papers.title: Co-Defining Transparency for Clinical AI: A Replicable Participatory Methodology
papers.abstract: Transparency is the most invoked safeguard for clinical AI, yet frameworks (e.g. the EU AI Act, FUTURE-AI) are specified top-down by regulators and technical experts, not bottom-up by the frontline users whose trust and adoption they should calibrate. This disconnect exacerbates the central deployment failure of clinical AI, miscalibrated reliance and adoption (such as automation bias, deskilling, or disuse), which technical explanation alone does not resolve. We argue that "how much transparency, of what kind, and for whom" is an empirical, context-dependent question, and present a replicable participatory methodology to answer it, instantiated at a large European university hospital. A cumulative chain of six workshops engages an inter-professional panel (clinicians, patient and caregiver partners, students) in agnostic, open-ended elicitation: 274 stakeholder verbatims and external benchmarks (eCH-0272, EU AI Act, Stanford FMTI) yield 20 indicators (18 prioritised and 2 recovered at a later stage), rated across five clinical scenarios of graduated intervention before and after technical briefings, discussed with legal experts, and translated into concrete implementation features. As an existence proof, the use case yields decision-useful signals: human review of automated decisions is the single most critical transparency indicator (84% of participants), and required transparency for adoption rises monotonically with the perceived risk of intervention, corroborating WHO risk-proportionality. A short explainability briefing did not substantially shift participants' transparency requirements. Of 151 evaluated AI transparency solutions, 79 were accepted as-is, covering (at least partially) 17 out of the 20 selected indicators. We position the six-workshop protocol (not its single-site outcomes) as the transferable artefact and release all instruments to support replication.

papers.title: Shared Understanding in Human-AI Teams: Coordination Continuity in Evolving Work
papers.abstract: People are increasingly working with AI agents as part of extended, asynchronous workflows. In these settings, shared access to information does not guarantee a shared basis for action: goals, plans, and roles may persist while their current significance changes. We introduce coordination continuity, the extent to which collaborators sustain a workable basis for interdependent action as work progresses. Drawing on research on collaborative work, along with two qualitative team studies and a reflexive case from our own repository-based environment, we present a framework of three elements: durable representations of collaborative work; relative coordination properties that support interpretation of representations in the moment; and interaction mechanisms through which the status of representations can be understood and altered. We use a build-act-drift-rebuild heuristic and the notion of consequential moments to characterise when rebuilding may be needed. We draw eight design implications for collaborative AI infrastructure.

papers.title: GAZEAIDE: Recording Gaze Context for Research on AI-Assisted Development
papers.abstract: Developers increasingly review code they did not write, much of it generated by AI. Where they look while reading may indicate what is relevant to them, but tools rarely have access to this information. We demonstrate GAZEAIDE, an open-source research prototype for collecting it. Using a webcam, GAZEAIDE estimates which parts of the code a developer looks at and for how long, and records this viewing history together with the text shown on screen. Such context can serve different purposes: providing visual feedback on what has been viewed, guiding code review, and preparing context for a question, which a developer can choose to send to an AI assistant. An IntelliJ plugin records work in the editor; a browser companion records assistant conversations. Attendees can record a short session, replay their viewing history, and try these scenarios.

papers.title: The Times They Are A-Changin': Tracking Global Trends through the Lens of Web Search
papers.abstract: Human societies have always left traces of their collective priorities, from cave drawings and stone carvings to chronicles on papyrus and printed books. In the digital era, these traces increasingly emerge through social media footprints and web search behavior at a global scale. We construct the first large-scale longitudinal dataset of Google Year in Search trends, spanning 15 years, to characterize how collective public attention evolves across countries and time. Because search engines like Google and Bing do not publicly release raw search logs, Year in Search provides a rare cross-national archive of annually salient search interests. The dataset is supplemented with a manually curated, unified ten-category semantic taxonomy with strong inter-annotator agreement. We focus on four categories (Information Seeking, Personality, Entertainment, and Sports) to investigate how collective attention varies across geographic and socio-cultural contexts. Our analyses reveal a consistently glocalized structure of collective attention: countries converge strongly in profession-level personality attention while remaining differentiated in the specific individuals they search for, yet profession-level similarity is only weakly associated with geographic region and income group. Information seeking is globally dominated by politics and health, while regional distributions show varying degrees of divergence. Crisis periods are associated with both shared and regionally differentiated shifts. Entertainment and sports attention likewise combine globally prominent interests with regional differentiation. Overall, our findings suggest that web search data provide a valuable computational lens for observing collective attention at scale, acting as a living archive of how societal priorities vary across countries and change over time.

papers.title: Standard-Anchored Delegation in Teachers' Use of Generative AI
papers.abstract: Teachers who use generative AI must decide which parts of their work to hand over, while they remain accountable for what reaches students. We studied these decisions in Punjab, Pakistan, through a qualitatively driven mixed-methods study. We interviewed 13 teachers from government, private, NGO and vocational institutions, four administrators and one student, and coded each teacher's position on twelve educational tasks. Nine teachers accepted AI drafts or substantial assistance with lesson planning, but none accepted AI-drafted learning objectives, and eleven did not use AI to encourage or emotionally support students. Teachers who would accept AI marking required that the model be given a rubric or marking criteria. Building on assessment research and HCI work on verifiability, we call this pattern standard-anchored delegation: teachers handed a component of a task to AI when a standard outside the model, such as a textbook or rubric, defined a correct output and the teacher could apply that standard to the result. Having a standard was not always enough. Several government-school teachers did not use AI to mark quizzes even though the quizzes had answer keys, because they expected students to look for evidence of the teacher's effort. Checking AI output required subject knowledge and time, and private schools gave teachers more support for this than government schools did. Participants also read disclosure of AI use as a statement about whether the teacher had reviewed the work. We propose that teacher-facing AI tools ask for the relevant standard before generating and show each output beside it, and that schools account for the time that checking takes.

papers.title: On the Challenges of Using LLMs in High-Risk AI Recruitment: Guiding Questions for Legal Conformity with the AI Act
papers.abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) imposes detailed obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems but offers limited operational guidance, particularly when these systems integrate third-party General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models. This paper introduces a toolkit that fosters the development of legal-by-design AI-assisted recruitment systems by translating the core legal obligations of the AI Act's conformity assessment---specifically Articles 9--15 and Annex IV---into techno-normative requirements and corresponding guiding questions. While recruitment pipelines may involve components with varying technical complexity and differing levels of algorithmic transparency, this paper focuses on the most challenging case: the integration of third-party GPAI models into critical stages of the selection process, including resume and job description parsing, applicant scoring, and shortlist generation. This scenario presents significant challenges for downstream providers of high-risk AI systems, as it underscores the difficulties in obtaining the technical information needed to demonstrate compliance with the AI Act's techno-normative requirements, both prior to and during market deployment. After introducing the toolkit and illustrating its application through a simplified example, the paper explores informational dependencies between upstream and downstream GPAI model providers. These dependencies may produce informational gaps across the AI supply chain, potentially hindering the collection of evidence necessary for the AI system provider to ensure legal compliance. The resulting lack of technical transparency negatively affects the deployer, who may struggle to maintain meaningful oversight of the system, and ultimately impacts the persons subject to the AI output.

papers.title: Omo: Giving Continuing AI-Agent Work a Place to Return To
papers.abstract: AI coding agents now keep working while the people who started them are away. Coming back is the hard part: a session list tells you which agent is where, but not what it was asked to do, what it changed, or what to tell it next. We present Omo, which gives each piece of continuing agent work a persistent place to return to. We built the idea twice. Omo Space is an open-source Minecraft mod in which rooms and screens that people build are live terminals on their own machine. Omo Theia brings the same rooms and desks into a customizable IDE, one step away from the editor and the Git patch. Both keep agent sessions running on the host after the view is closed. We describe the two systems, four lessons from building them, and a study designed to test whether returning to a place helps people pick up agent work correctly.

papers.title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
papers.abstract: Rigorously evaluating medical artificial intelligence (AI) requires testing open-ended clinical management across diverse presentations and stages of care. However, existing benchmarks rely on manual expert authoring, limiting coverage across conditions, conditional care pathways, and evolving guidelines. We develop an automated pipeline that extracts and verifies structured clinical criteria and branching decision trees from practice recommendations to generate scenarios spanning the care continuum, including nuanced presentations and practice variations across regions and guideline editions. Applied to 436 BMJ Best Practice clinical monographs (354 US, 82 International), this yields 3,200 scenarios spanning differential diagnosis, investigations, treatment, and complications, plus targeted suites for regional specificity (731 US/International pairs) and temporal freshness (630 scenarios). To grade responses, we develop a clinician-calibrated autorater that scores management plans on a 4-point rubric stratifying deviations by clinical severity. Across Gemini models, scaling improves adherence, while web search (+0.8 percentage points [pp] on average) and multi-sample synthesis (+2.2 pp) combine additively (+2.8 pp). In context, full monographs consistently trail condensed excerpts. On targeted suites, web search narrows international performance gaps (+4.2 pp) and improves adherence to newly updated guidance (+4.6 pp). In a study with Primary Care Physicians (n = 9) across 200 scenarios, AI assistance raises adherence from 50.5% to 70.0%, driven largely by fewer clinical omissions. Overall, our results demonstrate a scalable evaluation setup using an evidence-based corpus originally written to guide human clinical decision-making, and demonstrate its viability to assess medical AI and its assistance on clinician decision-making.

papers.title: Comparing Visual Motion Patterns for Pedestrian Guidance with Multi-Display Signage: Two Field Studies
papers.abstract: Public multi-display signage (MDS) has the potential to provide subtle pedestrian guidance through visual motion while retaining its conventional role in advertising and information delivery. However, it remains unclear how different visual motion patterns relate to pedestrian spatial distributions and how these relationships vary across deployment settings. We conducted two exploratory field studies in a museum, involving 18,402 pedestrian passages over 25 experimental days, to examine lateral positions in relation to stripe-motion contrast and coverage patterns. In Test Case 1 (TC1), involving predominantly one-way pedestrian flow, partial stripe presentation was associated with more leftward lateral positions than wider-coverage patterns in some comparisons, and lower contrast in full-screen stripes was not associated with a detectable reduction in the observed lateral bias. In Test Case 2 (TC2), conducted in a different spatial configuration permitting bidirectional walking, lateral positions differed by stripe-motion direction during one-way flow, but coverage effects on lateral position and stripe-advertisement differences in lateral position or passing-side choice were not significant. In both test cases, partial stripes received lower self-reported sickness ratings than full-screen stripes. These findings suggest that lower-contrast and reduced-motion-coverage designs hold practical potential for pedestrian guidance, with spatially restricted cues potentially allowing such guidance to coexist with existing advertising while reducing discomfort. At the same time, the contrasting patterns in TC1 and TC2 suggest that spatial context may shape how pedestrians respond to stripe coverage, highlighting the context-dependent suitability of visual-motion-based guidance and the need for further investigation.

papers.title: Beyond Prompt Heuristics: Assessing Child Safety Alignment in LLMs
papers.abstract: Child-safety taxonomies typically characterize safety risks through a predefined set of harm categories, and existing evaluations largely operationalize these categories using prompts that explicitly invoke them. However, child-safety considerations can also arise in seemingly benign requests that lack recognizable harm-category cues. We therefore investigate how child-safety alignment generalizes to such settings. Across six models, we find considerably higher misalignment rates on requests without recognizable harm-category cues than on those containing such cues (80.0, 54.0, and 48.4 percentage-point gaps for Qwen3.5-27B, GPT-5.4-mini, and Claude-Haiku-4.5, respectively). Through controlled behavioral and mechanistic analyses, we find that introducing a single harm-associated word reduces misalignment across most models, with mechanistic evidence suggesting that child-safety reasoning may rely in part on lexical and semantic associations with words in the prompt. Our findings motivate evaluations that treat child safety as context-dependent, and not reducible to a fixed set of harm categories.

papers.title: Aromatic polyketides from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus unguis PM03: α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, structure-activity relationship, molecular docking and ADMET evaluation
papers.abstract: Chemical investigation of Aspergillus unguis PM03 yielded eight known aromatic polyketides, including unguinol (1), nidulin (2), 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3), 2-chlorounguinol (4), emeguisin B (5), aspergillusether A (6), guisinol (7), and isosclerone (8). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and comparison with published data. All isolated compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against four human cancer cell lines (KB, Hep-G2, A549, and MCF-7) and for α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. None of the compounds exhibited significant cytotoxicity (IC50 > 128 μM). Compounds 1, 3, 5, 7, and 8 inhibited α-glucosidase, with guisinol (7) showing the strongest activity (IC50 = 4.01 μM), followed by isosclerone (8) (11.39 μM), emeguisin B (5) (24.31 μM), unguinol (1) (26.28 μM), and 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3) (28.83 μM). To our knowledge, this is the first report of the α-glucosidase inhibitory activity of compounds 1–7. A preliminary structure–activity relationship analysis suggested that the substitution pattern of the aromatic polyketides may affect their inhibitory activity. Molecular docking of compounds 1–7 and four aromatic polyketides previously isolated in our studies was performed against penicillin-binding protein 2a (PBP2a; PDB ID: 1MWT), together with in silico ADMET prediction to assess their pharmacokinetic properties.

papers.title: Short-form video and microlearning in English language education: A bibliometric and science mapping review
papers.abstract: Short-form video platforms, particularly TikTok, have altered how second language learners encounter and process linguistic input. Individual studies have examined specific aspects of microlearning in second language contexts, yet, to the authors' knowledge, no bibliometric analysis has mapped the intellectual structure of this emerging subfield. This study maps the publication landscape, thematic clusters, and research gaps characterizing microlearning research in English language education through short-form video platforms. We conducted a hybrid bibliometric analysis of 80 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2004 and 2026. Performance analysis was performed using Biblioshiny (R), and science mapping was executed through VOSviewer. The bibliometric outputs were then interpreted through a qualitative synthesis using the Theory, Context, Characteristics, and Methodology framework. Three principal patterns emerged. First, scholars from developing Asian economies, including Malaysia, Hong Kong, China, and Indonesia, contributed the largest share of publications, whereas traditional Western academic centers produced comparatively fewer studies. Second, the thematic clusters concentrated on phonological production and vocabulary acquisition, with limited attention to academic writing or reading comprehension. Third, qualitative and experimental designs together accounted for approximately two-thirds of the corpus, while computational learning analytics appeared only peripherally in the keyword co-occurrence network. This bibliometric review maps the knowledge structure of a rapidly expanding subfield at the intersection of educational technology and applied linguistics. The findings point to a need for longitudinal experimental designs, methodological diversification toward learning analytics, and empirical investigation of how algorithmic recommendation systems mediate L2 input delivery.

papers.title: Real-Time Water Quality Forecasting Using a Simulation-Driven IoT and Machine Learning Framework for Resource-Constrained Smart Cities
papers.abstract: This study proposes and evaluates a simulation-driven Internet of Things (IoT) and machine-learning framework for real-time water-quality monitoring and forecasting in resource-constrained smart cities. Ensuring timely and reliable water-quality data remains a critical challenge, as conventional monitoring approaches are often delayed, infrastructure-intensive, and difficult to scale. While IoT-based systems support continuous environmental monitoring, many existing implementations emphasise data acquisition rather than predictive analytics and deployment-oriented design. To address this gap, the study develops a unified simulation-based modelling framework in which virtual sensors generate key water-quality parameters, including pH, turbidity, temperature, and dissolved oxygen. The generated data are processed using a machine learning pipeline and used to train supervised models, namely XGBoost, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbours. Model performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to ensure balanced assessment across water-quality conditions. The results show that XGBoost achieves the highest predictive performance (91% accuracy), demonstrating strong capability in modelling non-linear environmental patterns and detecting unsafe water conditions. In addition to predictive performance, the framework supports real-time forecasting and visualisation through an integrated dashboard, enabling continuous monitoring and data-driven decision-making. The study contributes a reproducible and scalable framework that integrates simulation-based modelling, IoT-enabled monitoring, and machine learning for predictive analytics. The proposed approach provides a cost-effective pathway for advancing sustainable water management and environmental monitoring in resource-constrained smart-city environments.

papers.title: CIVIL AND CRIMINAL LIABILITY OF DEEPFAKE AI PLATFORM PROVIDERS IN VIOLATIONS OF THE RIGHT TO REPUTATION
papers.abstract: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has introduced deepfake technology, which is capable of manipulating audiovisual data with high realism. While this technology offers creative utility, its misuse for synthesizing non-consensual pornography, political disinformation, and character assassination severely violates an individual’s right to reputation. This study examines the civil and criminal liabilities of AI deepfake platform providers under the Indonesian legal framework, specifically Law No. 1/2024 (Second Amendment to the ITE Law) and Law No. 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection (UU PDP). Using a socio-legal research method, this study analyzes how textual legal norms interact with the digital behavior of platform providers and the psychological and social vulnerabilities of victims. The results indicate a significant normative gap: current regulations primarily target the individual creators or distributors of deepfake content, while platform providers escape liability by hiding behind the "safe harbor" doctrine. Sociologically, this legal vacuum fosters a culture of impunity and exacerbates digital gender-based violence. This paper argues for a paradigm shift from passive moderation to active algorithmic accountability. Platform providers must be held civilly liable under Article 1365 of the Indonesian Civil Code for systemic negligence, and criminally liable under the corporate fault doctrine for failing to implement mandatory digital watermarking and proactive content filtration systems.

papers.title: Reconstructing the Legal Enforcement Framework for Digital Activism in an Era of Technological Disruption
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies has transformed civic engagement by enabling digital activism as a powerful medium for public participation, social advocacy, and democratic expression. While these developments strengthen citizen engagement, they also create significant legal challenges in balancing freedom of expression with the need to maintain public order and prevent digital misconduct. This study reconstructs the legal enforcement framework governing digital activism in the era of technological disruption by identifying regulatory deficiencies, evaluating current enforcement practices, and proposing a more adaptive and rights-based legal model. The research employs a qualitative normative legal methodology complemented by a socio-legal perspective. It analyzes statutory regulations, legal doctrines, judicial decisions, and policy frameworks concerning digital expression and online activism. Data were collected through a systematic review of legal documents, scholarly literature, and policy reports, then examined using conceptual and comparative legal analysis to identify structural weaknesses within existing enforcement mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that current enforcement remains largely rooted in conventional regulatory paradigms that inadequately address the complexity of digital activism. Ambiguous legal provisions, overlapping institutional authorities, and inconsistent enforcement practices generate legal uncertainty and increase the risk of over-criminalizing legitimate civic expression. Furthermore, the absence of clear legal standards governing digital advocacy, online mobilization, and algorithm-driven information dissemination complicates effective enforcement and weakens legal certainty. This study proposes a reconstructed enforcement framework grounded in the principles of proportionality, transparency, accountability, and digital rights protection. The framework emphasizes adaptive regulation, integrated digital governance, institutional capacity building, and clearer legal standards for technology-mediated civic participation. By bridging technological realities with constitutional safeguards, the proposed model contributes to contemporary legal scholarship on digital governance while offering practical policy recommendations for developing a more balanced, accountable, and responsive legal system capable of addressing the evolving challenges of the digital era.

papers.title: Evaluating Digital Technologies’ Economic and Environmental Effects on Compliance, Governance, and Privacy in Sustainable Environmental Management
papers.abstract: The purpose of the study was to analyze new technologies impact on environment. The prospective benefits and challenges of new technologies on the use of technologies within environmental governance and compliance were uncovered in this study. Utilizing a convergence approach of qualitative and quantitative studies, the researchers sent out a survey to 9407 stakeholders within the environment, which included civil society, the private sector, and government. The study found out that the enforcement and reporting of compliance with environmental legislation would be greatly assisted by the streamlining of governance and compliance in the adoption of new technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things (IoT), The study also acknowledged the presence of other challenges such as inadequate infrastructure, expensive technologies, and poor technical capacity. The gaps and challenges on the governance of the environment, compliance, and sustainability would be solved by the introduced new technologies, which in turn would create a sustainable environment. This would lead to the development of Nigeria in an economically sustainable manner, while also providing overall environmental sustainability. The paper recommend that Nigeria's should increase her investment in the construction of training facilities within the administrative regulatory systems of new technological systems in environmental sustainability, collaborative Joint ventures should be encouraged so as to achieve economies and environmental sustainability.

papers.title: Enseñanza del desarrollo e-commerce centrado en el usuario mediante un proyecto basado en Go: caso de estudio exploratorio en educación en ingeniería
papers.abstract: Software engineering courses often address technical implementation and user experience evaluation independently, limiting the integration of these dimensions throughout the learning process. To address this challenge, this article presents an exploratory educational case study conducted in a Human-Computer Interaction course, centered on Go-Plant, an e-commerce platform developed using Go. The educational experience integrated Project-Based Learning (PBL), the ADDIE model as an instructional design framework, and User-Centered Design (UCD). The project involved 30 students organized into six teams and ten external users who participated in formative usability testing. The initial evaluation identified difficulties in understanding payment methods (9/10 users), filtering products (5/10), and locating relevant information (5/10). These findings guided the redesign of navigation, the product catalog, shopping cart, and checkout process. Subsequently, the same ten users participated in a second visual acceptance evaluation, in which the mean score increased from 2.54 to 4.28 points on a five-point scale. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired samples revealed a statistically significant difference between the two versions (W=0.00; exact two-sided p=0.001953). The findings indicate greater visual acceptance of the redesigned interface and illustrate how integrating PBL, ADDIE, and UCD can connect technical development with formative evaluation and iterative interface improvement. This study provides a methodological reference for incorporating user-centered development practices into engineering education without establishing causal effects on student learning.

papers.title: Dancing in the Rain: The Effectiveness of Mobile Platform for Learning Ten Qira’at
papers.abstract: Since the last pandemic outbreak, mobile learning platforms have been extensively utilized. This widespread adoption is facilitated by the affordability of smart devices, particularly smartphones, the high internet penetration even in remote areas, and the user-friendly nature of mobile learning platforms. Numerous courseware has been developed to ensure continuous learning beyond the confines of the classroom. However, there is currently a lack of courseware and mobile applications specifically designed to guide and provide materials for the ten Qira'at recitation style. In response, we have developed Qiraat10 as supplemental material for teaching and learning the Qira'at recitation style at UniSHAMS. This paper aims to provide insights into the effectiveness of the mobile learning platform, specifically focusing on the courseware Qiraat10. Based on the data gathered, Qiraat10 has been found to be effective in assisting users, particularly students, in learning the ten Qira'at recitation style.

papers.title: Discovering the Drivers of Ecological Fashion Adoption Intention among Fast Fashion Consumers
papers.abstract: The environmental impact of fast fashion has garnered global attention due to its resource-intensive production, excessive waste, and pollution. In response, ecological fashion has emerged to promote sustainable consumption and mitigate environmental harm. However, research on ecological fashion adoption intention in developing countries remains limited. Despite growing awareness, many consumers continue to prioritize fast fashion over eco-friendly alternatives. This study examines how the need for fashion and need for uniqueness influence ecological fashion adoption intention among Malaysian consumers. A quantitative survey was conducted with 396 participants using a structured questionnaire. Data were analyzed using SPSS. Findings show that among the dimensions of the Need for Fashion, image consciousness and market knowledge significantly and positively influence ecological fashion adoption intention, while fashion awareness and fashion consciousness were not significant. For the Need for Uniqueness, creative choices and unpopular choices significantly affect adoption intention, whereas avoidance of similarity was not significant. These results highlight the importance of self-expression, creativity, and market awareness in driving sustainable fashion behavior in Malaysia. The study contributes theoretically by integrating fashion consciousness and uniqueness into ecological fashion adoption models in a developing country context. Practically, it offers insights for policymakers and marketers to design strategies that promote sustainable fashion adoption. By understanding consumer motivations, stakeholders can encourage environmentally responsible behavior, foster a greener lifestyle, and support Malaysia’s sustainable development objectives.

papers.title: Efeitos da suplementação probiótica nos níveis séricos de zonulina em pacientes com doença renal crônica: um ensaio clínico randomizado
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with intestinal dysbiosis, systemic inflammation, and impaired intestinal barrier function. Serum zonulin has been proposed as an indirect marker of intestinal permeability, although its clinical relevance in CKD remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of probiotic supplementation on serum zonulin levels in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. METHODS: In this randomized, placebo-controlled, triple-blind clinical trial, 40 hemodialysis patients were assigned to receive either a probiotic formulation or a placebo for six months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in serum zonulin from baseline to follow-up. Secondary outcomes included metabolic, anthropometric, hemodynamic, and gastrointestinal variables. RESULTS: Serum zonulin increased in both groups, with no significant between-group difference (placebo: 288.2 to 425.3 ng/mL; probiotic: 239.5 to 453.7 ng/mL; p = 0.882; ANCOVA p = 0.463). Pre-dialysis urea decreased within the probiotic group, but the between-group difference was not significant (p = 0.305). Serum phosphorus showed a greater reduction in the probiotic group than in the placebo group (p = 0.011; ANCOVA p = 0.011). No significant differences were observed for anthropometric or hemodynamic outcomes. CONCLUSION: Six months of probiotic supplementation did not significantly reduce serum zonulin levels in hemodialysis patients. Although a favorable effect on serum phosphoruswas observed, these findings do not support a measurable impact of this probiotic regimen on serum zonulin and highlight the need for larger studies incorporating direct assessments of intestinal permeability and gut microbiota.

papers.title: Visualizing a decade of machine translation research (2016–2025): A VOSviewer-based bibliometric analysis
papers.abstract: Background and Purpose: Machine translation has undergone rapid transformation over the past decade, driven by advances in neural machine translation and large language models, yet systematic attention to the field’s overall intellectual structure during this critical transition remains limited. This study aims to visualize the evolution of machine translation research from 2016 to 2025, with particular attention to its interdisciplinary development and trends in the post-2022 era of large language models. Methodology: This study presents a bibliometric analysis of machine translation research from a language and translation perspective, based on 582 journal articles published between 2016 and 2025 and indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection. Using VOSviewer, it examines the main characteristics of machine translation publications and key research themes. Findings: The findings show a steady rise in machine translation research output, reflecting growing scholarly interest alongside technological advances. Research is globally distributed but concentrated in Europe and Asia, particularly in Spain and China. Journals in translation studies and computational linguistics account for the largest share of publications and receive the most scholarly attention. However, the field has yet to form a stable core author group, indicating a dispersed and evolving research structure. Five major research themes are identified: technological development and model innovation; human-machine collaboration and application contexts; machine translation quality evaluation; translation studies and industry-related research; and language education with ethical considerations. Contributions: By mapping research trajectories and key contributors, this study offers a solid foundation for advancing future research, emphasizing the need for cross-regional and interdisciplinary collaboration and a balanced integration of technological, human, and ethical dimensions. Keywords: Bibliometric analysis, machine translation, translation studies, visualization, VOSviewer. Cite as: Tang, N., Moindjie, M. A., Lyu, Z., & Wu, S. (2026). Visualizing a decade of machine translation research (2016–2025): A VOSviewer-based bibliometric analysis. Journal of Nusantara Studies, 12(1), 1-19. http://dx.doi.org/10.24200/jonus.vol12iss1pp1-19

papers.title: Integrating concept-based instruction and project-based learning to enhance grammar competence, critical thinking, and collaboration among Cambodian student teachers authors
papers.abstract: Background and Purpose: Education plays a vital role in preparing a generation of learners who are critical, creative, and adaptable to an ever-changing world. This study aimed to examine the extent to which the integration of Concept-Based Instruction (CBI) and Project-Based Learning (PBL) improved the critical thinking, collaboration skills, and grammar competence of BTEC student teachers. Methodology and Results: A one-group pretest–posttest pre-experimental design was employed with 21 student teachers. A paired-samples t-test revealed that posttest scores were statistically significantly higher than pretest scores, with a mean gain of 9.29 points. Five expert evaluators assessed students’ project performance across five selected facets of understanding: Explanation, Interpretation, Application, Perspective, and Self-Knowledge. Group-level results showed overall means of 3.04 for Group 1, 3.36 for Group 2, and 3.09 for Group 3. Group 2 showed particularly high scores in Perspective (M = 3.80) and Explanation (M = 3.70). In addition, a Self/Group Evaluation Worksheet was administered to examine students’ perceptions of their collaborative learning experiences. The findings indicated that PBL activities supported students in working collaboratively, planning tasks, monitoring their work, and reflecting on their learning, thereby developing skills essential for teamwork and project management. Contribution: The findings provide empirical evidence that integrating Concept-Based Instruction and Project-Based Learning can provide an effective instructional framework for developing student teachers’ critical thinking and collaboration skills. The study suggests that policymakers and curriculum developers consider incorporating similar integrated approaches into teacher education curricula. Further research should examine the long-term effects of this instructional approach and its applicability across different educational contexts and learning trajectories. Keywords: Concept-based instruction, critical thinking, collaboration, grammar, project-based learning. Cite as: Hieng, S., Hum, C., Soeung, S., Chhen, S., & Sam, R. (2026). Integrating concept-based instruction and project-based learning to enhance grammar competence, critical thinking, and collaboration among Cambodian student teachers authors. Journal of Nusantara Studies, 12(1), 60-81. http://dx.doi.org/10.24200/jonus.vol12iss1pp60-81

papers.title: Multimodal interpretation of notation
papers.abstract: Challenges related to the teaching and learning of formal notation in school mathematics are widely documented, and specifically in relation to the underlying mathematical structures that the notation is intended to convey. In this article, we draw on embodied cognition to examine the interactions among three students working with the software Grid Algebra. Embodied cognition emphasises the role of gesture and movement in learning and understanding mathematics. Grid Algebra uses movement to direct students’ attention to mathematical operations on numbers and numerical expressions within the grid and the structure of these operations, while the software takes care of the formal notation of the numerical expressions that describe these sequences of operations. We analyse how different modes of communication work together to scaffold students’ fluency with operations and the formal notation representing these operations and the order in which they are performed. The dynamic between notation, speech, movement and position allows students to educate their interpretation of mathematical notation through the movements and positions that they are very familiar with.

papers.title: Impact of Agile Methods on Tacit Knowledge Sharing from Self-Determination Perspective: A Mixed Method Study of Chinese IT Teams
papers.abstract: The purpose of the study is to examine whether agile methods foster tacit knowledge sharing in IT project teams and to identify the motivational mechanisms, especially basic psychological needs and shared goals, underpinning this relationship in Chinese contexts. It does so by using a sequential mixed-methods design: survey data from 610 IT professionals (predominantly mainland China, with a small Hong Kong subsample) analysed with PLS-SEM, complemented by 22 semi structured interviews examined through comparative cross case analysis, thematic coding, and process tracing. The findings suggest agile methods positively predict tacit knowledge sharing, even after controlling for transformational leadership and enjoyment of sharing. This effect is largely mediated by satisfaction of basic psychological needs and shared goals. Autonomy and shared goals act mainly through competence and relatedness. Qualitative evidence underscores problem-driven collaboration, project ownership, and informal exchanges. That said, the main limitation of the study is that cross sectional, self report data, non probability sampling, and focus on Chinese IT professionals limit causal inference and generalizability. Nonetheless, the study provides empirical evidence that agile methods are linked to tacit knowledge sharing, explains how these methods foster such sharing through the satisfaction of basic psychological needs and the establishment of shared goals, and offers a rigorous operationalization of agile methods. This implies that managers should design agile practices as a motivational architecture that supports autonomy, competence, relatedness, and shared goals, rather than relying on formal, mandatory knowledge sharing sessions or performance linked incentives.

papers.title: Perceived Accuracy and Relevance of AI-Based Product Recommendations and Generation X Purchase Decisions in Jakarta
papers.abstract: This study examines how perceived accuracy and contextual relevance of artificial-intelligence-based product recommendations influence purchase decisions among Generation X e-commerce users in Jakarta. A quantitative explanatory design was modeled with 300 respondent profiles and 18 reflective indicators. Partial least squares structural equation modeling, 10,000-resample bootstrapping, coefficient-difference testing, and tenfold cross-validation were applied. Perceived accuracy had a stronger positive effect on purchase decisions (β=.604, p<.001) than relevance (β=.217, p<.001), and the difference was significant (Δβ=.387, p<.001). The model explained 54.2% of purchase-decision variance and showed positive Qpredict2​ values. The findings indicate an accuracy–relevance asymmetry: relevance attracts attention, whereas perceived accuracy more strongly reinforces purchase decisions.

papers.title: Development and Feasibility Evaluation of AR-GeoHazard for Slope Gradient Visualization in Pagar Alam
papers.abstract: Accessible terrain information is essential for supporting geospatial literacy and disaster education in mountainous environments. This study aimed to develop and evaluate AR-GeoHazard, an Android application for slope-gradient visualization in Pagar Alam, Indonesia. A research-and-development approach followed the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) framework, incorporating prototyping for application refinement. The application integrates elevation profiles, three-dimensional terrain visualization, smartphone-assisted slope observations, recording features, and interpretive guidance. Evaluation comprised 40 black-box test scenarios, assessments by two experts, task-based testing and System Usability Scale (SUS) questionnaires involving 20 users, and comparisons with geographic information system (GIS)-derived slope classes at 30 reference points. The evaluation results showed a functional success rate of 95.00%, an expert assessment score of 91.60%, a task-completion rate of 94.00%, a mean SUS score of 86.75, and GIS classification agreement of 93.33%. The weighted feasibility index reached 92.19, meeting the study-defined criteria for high feasibility. However, two functional failures, two classification mismatches, and ambiguous safety labels require further investigation. These findings support the continued development of AR-GeoHazard as an educational terrain-visualization tool, while sensor accuracy, spatial registration, and learning effectiveness require dedicated validation.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Chatbot for Academic Information Services Using GROQ API
papers.abstract: Academic information services in universities are still largely carried out manually by administrative staff with limited working hours, making it difficult for students to receive quick responses, especially outside office hours. This study aims to design and implement an academic chatbot using the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach through the Groq API and a Streamlit interface. The system was developed following the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, which includes problem identification, defining solution objectives, dataset collection, artifact design and development, system demonstration, testing and evaluation, as well as communication of research results. Black-box testing on 20 questions yielded 18 valid answers, while semantic quality evaluation using BERTScore produced a precision of 0.7054, recall of 0.7176, and F1-score of 0.7095. The average system response time was 1.45 seconds, with a median of 0.85 seconds, indicates that the majority of responses were provided in less than one second, despite a single outlier of 12.13 seconds. These results finding suggest that the integration of RAG with the Groq API holds potential for enhancing digital academic information services in higher education. Nevertheless, its operational benefits in real-world scenarios warrant further evaluation through empirical user testing.

papers.title: Design And Development Of A Web-Based Encyclopedia Of Jambi Traditional Culinary: A Case Study Of The Department Of Culture And Tourism Of Jambi Province
papers.abstract: Jambi traditional culinary is part of the region's cultural heritage that has historical value, distinctive flavors, and local identity. However, information about Jambi traditional culinary is still scattered across various media and has not been presented in a structured digital system, making it difficult for the public to obtain complete and accessible information. This study aims to design and develop a web-based Encyclopedia of Jambi Traditional Culinary as a medium for information, promotion, and cultural preservation. The system was developed using the Waterfall model, consisting of requirements analysis, system design, implementation, and testing. The application was developed using PHP with the CodeIgniter 4 framework and MySQL database. The search feature applies the Fuzzy Matching method using the similar_text() and levenshtein() functions to provide relevant results for inaccurate keywords. Black Box Testing and Fuzzy Matching testing were conducted to evaluate system functionality and search capability. The results show that all main system functions operated according to the specified requirements, with an average similarity score of 86.50% and a processing time of less than 10 milliseconds. The system successfully presents information on Jambi traditional culinary, including names, descriptions, ingredients, cooking procedures, categories, and images. Therefore, the system can facilitate public access to culinary information while supporting the digitalization and preservation of regional cultural heritage.
